e-4910.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of a Line Given in Canonical Form
e-4910.problem: Consider the straight line with the canonical equation $\dfrac{x}{5}=\dfrac{y+3}{3}=\dfrac{z-2}{1}.$ Find the vector equation of the line.
e-4910.worked_solution:
Remember that the Cartesian (canonical) equation of the straight line that passes through the point $P(x_0,y_0,z_0)$ and is parallel to the vector $\mathbf{v}=\langle v_x, v_y, v_z \rangle$ is given by

$$
\dfrac{x-x_0}{v_x}=\dfrac{y-y_0}{v_y}=\dfrac{z-z_0}{v_z} = t, \qquad t \in (-\infty,\infty).
$$

Comparing the above to our given equation

$$
\dfrac{x}{5}=\dfrac{y-(-3)}{3}=\dfrac{z-2}{1},
$$

we find that our line passes through the point $P(0,-3,2)$ and is parallel to $\mathbf{v}=\langle 5,3,1 \rangle.$ Therefore, its vector equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Consider the straight line with the canonical equation $\frac{x-3}{5}=\frac{y-1}{1}=\frac{z+7}{-5}.$ Find the vector equation of the line.
after.worked_solution:
Remember that the Cartesian (canonical) equation of the straight line that passes through the point $P({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ and is parallel to the vector $v=⟨{v}_{x},{v}_{y},{v}_{z}⟩$, is given by

$$
\frac{x-{x}_{0}}{{v}_{x}}=\frac{y-{y}_{0}}{{v}_{y}}=\frac{z-{z}_{0}}{{v}_{z}}=t,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

Comparing the above to our given equation

$$
\frac{x-3}{5}=\frac{y-1}{1}=\frac{z-(-7)}{-5},
$$

we find that our line passes through the point $P(3,1,-7)$ and is parallel to $v=⟨5,1,-5⟩.$ Therefore, its vector equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ -7\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1 \\ -5\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem: Consider the straight line with the canonical equation $\frac{x-3}{5}=\frac{y-1}{1}=\frac{z+7}{-5}.$ Find the vector equation of the line.
content.worked_solution:
Remember that the Cartesian (canonical) equation of the straight line that passes through the point $P({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ and is parallel to the vector $v=⟨{v}_{x},{v}_{y},{v}_{z}⟩$, is given by

$$
\frac{x-{x}_{0}}{{v}_{x}}=\frac{y-{y}_{0}}{{v}_{y}}=\frac{z-{z}_{0}}{{v}_{z}}=t,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

Comparing the above to our given equation

$$
\frac{x-3}{5}=\frac{y-1}{1}=\frac{z-(-7)}{-5},
$$

we find that our line passes through the point $P(3,1,-7)$ and is parallel to $v=⟨5,1,-5⟩.$ Therefore, its vector equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ -7\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1 \\ -5\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: Find the parametric equations of the line $\frac{x-10}{7}=\frac{y+8}{-4}=\frac{z+1}{11}.$
after.worked_solution:
Remember that the Cartesian (canonical) equation of the straight line that passes through the point $P({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ and is parallel to the vector $v=⟨{v}_{x},{v}_{y},{v}_{z}⟩$, is given by

$$
\frac{x-{x}_{0}}{{v}_{x}}=\frac{y-{y}_{0}}{{v}_{y}}=\frac{z-{z}_{0}}{{v}_{z}}=t,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

Comparing the above to our given equation

$$
\frac{x-10}{7}=\frac{y-(-8)}{-4}=\frac{z-(-1)}{11},
$$

we find that our line passes through the point $P(10,-8,-1)$ and is parallel to $v=⟨7,-4,11⟩.$ Therefore, its vector equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}10 \\ -8 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -4 \\ 11\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations are the following:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=10+7t \\ y=-8-4t \\ z=-1+11t\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem: Find the parametric equations of the line $\frac{x-10}{7}=\frac{y+8}{-4}=\frac{z+1}{11}.$
content.worked_solution:
Remember that the Cartesian (canonical) equation of the straight line that passes through the point $P({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ and is parallel to the vector $v=⟨{v}_{x},{v}_{y},{v}_{z}⟩$, is given by

$$
\frac{x-{x}_{0}}{{v}_{x}}=\frac{y-{y}_{0}}{{v}_{y}}=\frac{z-{z}_{0}}{{v}_{z}}=t,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

Comparing the above to our given equation

$$
\frac{x-10}{7}=\frac{y-(-8)}{-4}=\frac{z-(-1)}{11},
$$

we find that our line passes through the point $P(10,-8,-1)$ and is parallel to $v=⟨7,-4,11⟩.$ Therefore, its vector equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}10 \\ -8 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -4 \\ 11\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations are the following:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=10+7t \\ y=-8-4t \\ z=-1+11t\end{aligned}
$$
